title: Ukraine Launches 347-Drone Mass Attack Across 20 Russian Regions — Second-Largest Drone Barrage of the War, Shutting Down Moscow Airports
detail: Overnight on May 6-7, 2026, Ukraine launched its second-largest aerial drone attack of the war, with Russia's Defense Ministry reporting 347 Ukrainian drones intercepted across 20 Russian regions including Moscow Oblast. The attack disrupted air traffic at all three major Moscow airports — Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo, and Vnukovo — with nearly 100 flights delayed or canceled by midday on May 7. Ukraine framed the attack as a direct, symmetrical response to Russia's rejection of Ukraine's open-ended ceasefire and continued strikes on Ukrainian civilians (27 killed May 5). President Zelensky confirmed the operation, stating: 'Russia rejected the ceasefire. Russia continues to hit Ukrainian cities. Ukraine will act symmetrically.' Russia's MoD reported its air defense systems destroyed 347 drones in the overnight operation, though Ukrainian sources reported damage to Russian military and infrastructure targets. The attack was the largest on Russia since Ukraine's record 389-drone barrage in March 2026. The scale of the Ukrainian drone campaign has consistently forced Russia to allocate substantial air defense resources to protecting its interior, diverting them from front-line use.

media.caption: Ukraine launches 347-drone attack across 20 Russian regions overnight, disrupting all three Moscow airports — a direct response to Russia's ceasefire violations on May 6

title: Russia Kills 2 in Sumy Kindergarten Strike, Wounds 9 (Including 3 Children) in Kharkiv — Sumy Declares Day of Mourning
detail: On May 7, 2026, Russian forces struck a kindergarten in Ukraine's Sumy border region, killing 2 people — an attack that prompted Sumy city authorities to declare a day of mourning. Russian forces also launched a drone strike on residential Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, wounding 9 people including 3 children. Across the Sumy border region, Russian forces launched at least 65 airstrikes dropping 178 guided aerial bombs and deployed 4,869 kamikaze drones throughout May 7 (Day 1,534 of the war). Ukraine's air defense shot down 92 of 102 Russian drones in one overnight wave. On the ground, Russian forces conducted 156 combat engagements across all fronts, including 21 assault actions in the Pokrovsk direction, 17 attacks toward Huliaipole (Zaporizhzhia region), and 8 assaults near Lyman (Donetsk region). Russia's strikes on the Sumy region came despite a 5 km buffer zone agreed in late 2024; Ukrainian border authorities documented the zone as routinely violated. The kindergarten strike, targeting civilian infrastructure during a declared ceasefire period, was condemned by Ukrainian officials as a deliberate war crime.

media.caption: Russia strikes Sumy kindergarten killing 2, wounds 9 in Kharkiv including children — attacks continue despite both sides' declared ceasefires heading into Victory Day

title: Russia Warns Foreigners to Leave Kyiv, Threatens Massive Missile Strike on City Center Before Victory Day — Dueling Ceasefires Collapse
detail: On May 7, 2026, Russia issued warnings to foreign nationals and embassy staff in Kyiv to evacuate the city, citing a threat of a 'massive missile strike on the center of Kyiv' if Ukraine conducted attacks on Russian territory during the Victory Day holiday period (May 8-9). The warnings, delivered through diplomatic back-channels and Russian state media, marked one of the most direct open threats against Kyiv since the opening days of the full-scale invasion. The threat came as both competing ceasefire declarations collapsed: Ukraine's open-ended ceasefire (started midnight May 6) had been violated by Russia within minutes, with 1,820 violations documented by 10 AM May 6. Russia's unilateral Victory Day ceasefire (covering only May 8-9) was itself violated simultaneously, with continuous Russian combat operations throughout the period. Defense News reported both ceasefires had 'collapsed almost immediately' amid mutual accusations. Zelensky stated Russia had 'not stopped any type of military activity' and Ukraine would act symmetrically. The Kremlin claimed Ukraine was using the period to attack Russian targets, citing the 347-drone barrage as evidence of Ukrainian bad faith. Western analysts viewed the competing ceasefire declarations as a propaganda battle rather than genuine de-escalation — three rounds of US-mediated talks in the UAE and Switzerland (January-February 2026) had already failed to produce any framework.

media.caption: Russia warns foreigners to leave Kyiv and threatens a massive missile strike on the city center ahead of Victory Day as both dueling ceasefire declarations collapse
